newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends lower on spillover from beans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends lower on spillover from beans.

text.p: CBOT rice futures closed lower Tuesday in line with losses in the soybean and grain pits, floor sources said.
"The market is really looking for direction," a floor source said.
Losses were limited by strong commercial buying beneath the market and export demand was said to be picking up. Traders said Peru bought 5,000 tonnes U.S. brown rice for April 10-May 5 shipment.
There was talk Colombia was also in the market for U.S. rice but export sources could not confirm the deal.
New-crop months drew support from forecasts for another week of cold, wet weather in key southern growing states.

"The six- to 10-day (National Weather Service) forecast looks kind of iffy," a trader said. "We're just now entering the optimal planting period in Arkansas and Mississippi. If it stays cold and wet like this for a few more weeks, we'll be in real trouble."
Rice ended 5-1/2 to one cent lower, with May off 5-1/2 at $11.26-1/2 per cwt.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 250 lots against Monday's actual volume of 400 lots.
